newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria mulls changes to deposit guarantee law.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria mulls changes to deposit guarantee law.

text.p: Bulgaria plans to amend a recently approved deposit guarantee law to avoid a fresh rise in state spending in case of opening new bankruptcy procedures against ailing local banks, officials said.

"So far we have several optons for amending the (deposit guarantee) law and the central bank and the government have to make a decision as soon as possible," a Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) official, who declined to be named, told Reuters. @

Amendment options varied from reduction of state guarantee to 20 percent of deposits to issuing seven-year government bonds to depositors against their savings in banks that might be closed down, the BNB official said.
"It is very risky to burden the state budget further because the state already has to service a domestic debt of more than 500 billion levs," a finance ministry official told Reuters.
The law was approved by the parliament in May to protect depositors' money in five local banks, against which the BNB opened bankruptcy procedures through the courts. @
The law provides for a 100 percent state guarantee on personal savings in those banks and 50 percent coverage of companies' deposits.

Under the law the government issued treasury bonds worth a total of 80 billion levs and $100 million, which were placed with the State Savings Bank and the state-owned Bulgarian Post Bank to guarantee payments to depositors in the five banks.
For this year alone the budget has to pay interest of 8.5 billion levs on treasury paper issued under the law.
Bulgaria's goverment debt amounted to 582.5 billion levs at the end of July. @
"So far only one point concerning the amendments is certain - that the state guarantee on deposits will go in force only after a court opens a bankruptcy procedure for a bank," the BNB official said.
Under the current law new accounts for depositors were opened into the SSB and the Post Bank immediately after the central bank asked the court to open bankruptcy procedures against the five banks. @
So far the central bank has initiated procedures against the state-owned Mineralbank, First Private Bank, the private Agrobusinessbank and Krystalbank and Private Agricultural and Investment Bank.
"The central bank will carry on its restrictive money policy and if it is necessary it will seek new bank closures," the BNB governor Lyubomir Filipov told the national radio on Monday. @
Eighteen undercapitalised commercial banks signed memorandums of understanding with the central bank in July, pledging to raise their capital-to-assets ratio and tighten lending discipline.

"So far only several (of those banks) have shown positive results but the majority have made no progress with three or four of them even in a worse condition than at the end of June," a central bank official said.
He declined to name the banks but added that the BNB could slap tough restrictions on them, including a ban on lending and putting them under a special supervision. @
An IMF mission last week urged Bulgaria to restore public confidence in local troubled banks by stabilising its financial system. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
